message.content: {"skills": [{"category": "characterization", "trigger": "When evaluating a thoracic mass on a lateral chest X-ray to determine if it originates from the lung parenchyma or extrapulmonary structures (e.g., pleura, chest wall, mediastinum).", "steps": ["Inspect the interface between the mass and the adjacent chest wall (ribs/sternum/spine) or mediastinum on the lateral projection.", "Assess the angle formed by the mass margin and the surface it abuts: an obtuse angle (>90 degrees) with a broad base suggests an extrapulmonary origin, whereas an acute angle (<90 degrees) typically indicates a pulmonary parenchymal origin.", "Evaluate the margins: well-circumscribed, smooth borders favor extrapulmonary lesions (like pleural tumors), while irregular or spiculated margins often suggest primary lung malignancy."]}]}
